Vendored win-iconv 0.0.8
========================

Locked dependency providing the POSIX iconv API (iconv_open/iconv/
iconv_close) on Windows, where the platform ships no system iconv. Used by
src/txiki_restricted_core.c for the restricted TextDecoder encoding path
(arbitrary codepage -> UTF-8). Linux and macOS keep their system iconv
via find_package(Iconv); this tree is authoritative and the build never
downloads it at configure time.

Provenance
----------

- Upstream:   https://github.com/win-iconv/win-iconv
- Locked tag: v0.0.8
- Files:      https://github.com/win-iconv/win-iconv/tree/v0.0.8

Copied verbatim from the tag, unmodified:

- iconv.h
- win_iconv.c
- readme.txt

License: public domain ("win_iconv is placed in the public domain",
readme.txt). The upstream implementation converts via the Win32
MultiByteToWideChar/WideCharToMultiByte APIs and does NOT perform strict
encoding validation (readme.txt: "This implementation cannot be used for
encoding validation purpose") — Capsid uses it for decoding only, never
as a byte-validity authority.

Build contract
--------------

- Built only on WIN32 (cmake/build_worker.cmake) as the `capsid_winiconv`
  static library aliased to Iconv::Iconv; never built on POSIX platforms.
- Compiled with the project's C baseline; vendor sources are intentionally
  NOT built with the project's strict-warnings regime, so upstream
  warnings can never block the build.

Upgrade checklist
-----------------

1. Replace iconv.h, win_iconv.c and readme.txt from the new tag.
2. Update this file (tag) before committing.
3. Re-run the Windows build and the TextDecoder-related worker tests.
